newsitem.title: TANZANIA: U.N. Rwanda trial hears journalist's evidence.
newsitem.headline: U.N. Rwanda trial hears journalist's evidence.

text.p: The U.N. tribunal for Rwanda heard testimony on Friday from a British correspondent who said she watched hundreds of bodies pile up in Kigali at the start of the 1994 genocide.

Lindsey Hilsum of the British Broadcasting Corporation was one of the few correspondents in the Rwandan capital on April 6 1994, when the mass killings began, and told the court how she saw a huge pile of bodies outside Kigali central hospital.

"There was a big pile like a mountain outside and these were bodies with slash wounds, with heads smashed in, many of them were naked," she said. She estimated there were around 500 bodies in the pile.
She said she saw many more corpses while touring the streets and spoke to colleagues and friends by telephone who described other killings in Kigali.
Hilsum, the prosecution's fifth witness and the second expert witness, did not mention the accused, Jean-Paul Akayesu, 43, in her evidence.
But her evidence is key to the prosecution which must prove Akayesu participated in the government-led genocide of Rwanda's Tutsi minority and moderate members of the Hutu majority.

Akayesu, the former mayor of Rwanda's central Taba commune, has pleaded not guilty to charges of genocide and crimes against humanity. If convicted he faces life imprisonment, the tribunal's higest penalty.
